RNA-C1.target: Explain the emergence and persistence of internal RNA-poor cavities as measured by the arithmetic mean per-droplet hollow-area ratio f(t), and make a mechanism-level prediction that can distinguish composition-linked demixing from a reaction-condition/carryover pathway.
known_relations: Observed non-reference DNA read fraction is 0.0500 among listed reads; total listed plus reference is 0.9966. Read fraction is not RNA yield or active-valence fraction (sequence_measurements.json; C01).
Observed endpoint hollow-area ratio differs across purified template-length fractions M, M+L, M+S (fraction_dev.json/E02); exact composition and matched carryover are absent.

Observed measured reference and variant RNA concentrations in dense and dilute phases yield tie-line-specific partition ratios (C04); these are endpoint measurements and do not determine cavity formation.
Observed tracking lacks persistent per-droplet cavity state and area trajectories (C03).
Interpretation: B condition is associated with the later increase in f; causal effect of amplification, template heterogeneity, and carryover remains unidentified.

hypotheses.statement: If transcription produces two RNA populations with different effective interaction valence, their accumulating mixture can cross a composition-dependent coexistence boundary inside an initially RNA-rich condensate. Selective partitioning then enriches one population in the outer dense phase and stabilizes an internal RNA-poor phase; the hollow-area ratio rises when the local composition crosses the boundary. The novel bridge proposed here is composition-dependent internal demixing coupled to selective phase partitioning, rather than a direct inference from DNA length or read frequency.
hypotheses.status_note: Untested hypothesis. No supplied evidence establishes that any listed sequence variant changes effective valence, RNA production, partitioning in the cavity, coexistence boundary, or image area.

hypotheses.statement: Amplification-associated reaction carryover or another changed reaction condition alters transcription, ionic environment, or condensate organization and drives the hollow-area change without sequence composition being the causal mediator.

gaps.description: No supported constitutive relation maps RNA species composition and tie-line-dependent partitioning to the onset, persistence, or area fraction of internal cavities.
No matched measurement links template composition to transcribed RNA composition over time; DNA read frequencies cannot substitute for RNA concentrations.
The image statistic has no validated mapping to phase volume, local concentration, or single-droplet cavity dynamics.

variables_units.meaning: concentration of RNA species i in dense phase

variables_units.name: c_i^L
variables_units.meaning: concentration of RNA species i in dilute phase

variables_units.name: K_i
variables_units.meaning: partition ratio c_i^D/c_i^L on a specified tie-line

variables_units.name: phi
variables_units.meaning: internal RNA-poor phase volume fraction, latent and not measured

variables_units.name: x_star
variables_units.meaning: hypothesized local mixture threshold for internal demixing

equations: K_i = c_i^D / c_i^L when c_i^L > 0; undefined when the denominator is zero.
For a closed two-species equilibrium mixture only, x_V^D = (K_V x_V^L) / (K_V x_V^L + K_R (1 - x_V^L)); this is a compositional consequence of partition ratios, not a kinetic or cavity model.

H1 threshold statement: phi = 0 for x_V^D < x_star and phi > 0 may occur for x_V^D >= x_star. This is a deliberately minimal phenomenological hypothesis; no supplied data identify x_star or the function phi(x_V^D).
Observation mapping is unknown: f = h(phi, cavity geometry, droplet selection, segmentation) and cannot be set equal to phi without additional evidence.

parameters_ranges.name: K_R, K_V
parameters_ranges.range: Use only the supplied tie-line-specific estimates and error rectangles in C04; do not pool tie-lines or interpret the rectangles as confidence intervals.

initial_boundary_conditions: At t=0 the observed group means are similar, but this does not establish identical microscopic state or composition.
For H1, initial local x_V^D is assumed below x_star only as a conditional scenario; this is not observed.
No time-resolved RNA production, phase volumes, phase fluxes, or cavity-specific concentration boundary conditions are supplied.
observation_mapping: Observed f is a mean of object-level area ratios, not concentration, phase volume fraction, or thermodynamic order parameter.
C04 ng/uL phase concentrations cannot be directly converted to f without geometry, phase volumes, and spatially matched imaging.
Object counts and field SEM do not supply independent-preparation uncertainty.
alternatives: H2 reaction carryover or altered reaction conditions change transcription or condensate organization without sequence mediation.
Population selection, droplet coalescence, or object detection changes aggregate f; C03 does not provide longitudinal state/area trajectories to test this.
Segmentation or sampling changes the measured f; supplied data do not quantify robustness to thresholds.

predictions.statement: At fixed reaction chemistry and total RNA production, increasing the measured variant RNA fraction across a threshold should increase the probability of cavity-bearing droplets or their object-level hollow-area ratio under H1; H2 predicts no systematic dependence on variant fraction once carryover and reaction conditions are matched.
predictions.measure: Independently quantify transcribed RNA composition and per-droplet hollow-area ratio in a composition series, with matched carryover and independent preparations.
predictions.limitation: No new physical experiment is available in this run; current endpoint length-fraction data are not a controlled composition series.

predictions.statement: If C04 tie-line partition ratios apply to the relevant mixture and both species are present, changing x_V^L can change x_V^D nonlinearly; this can shift a threshold x_star. The direction is conditional on the applicable tie-line and cannot be inferred by pooling the three tie-lines.

checks: Dimensional check: K_i, x_V, x_star, phi, and f are dimensionless; concentrations in C04 share ng/uL units.
Zero-denominator check: variant K on tie-line 0 is undefined, not zero or infinity.
Limit check: if K_V = K_R and both species are present, the partition equation gives x_V^D = x_V^L; if x_V^L approaches 0 or 1, x_V^D approaches the same endpoint.
Balance/closure check: the partition equation is an equilibrium composition identity under a closed two-species assumption; it does not close time-dependent mass balance or predict cavities.
Numerical check: no new numerical calculation was performed in this leader reply; all listed values are supplied C01-C04 results.
evidence_conflicts: Length-fraction endpoints are compatible with composition dependence but do not establish its cause; reaction carryover and exact RNA composition are unmeasured.
Tie-line partition ratios vary substantially and have broad marginal error rectangles; their tie-line conditions are not mapped to B's time course.
The 36/48 h C02 predictions differ by model form and are descriptive extrapolations only.
untested: Whether the length variants produce RNA at comparable rates or persist in RNA.
Whether sequence differences change effective valence, phase partition, or internal coexistence.
Whether internal dark areas are an RNA-poor phase rather than another optical/structural state.
Whether increasing f reflects same-droplet cavity growth versus population and measurement effects.
Whether any target-specific literature directly supports or contradicts H1.

T05.acceptance: Return dated source IDs and the actual supported relation (not references-only); state full-text versus abstract support; explicitly assess applicability to internally cavitating RNA condensates; give a dimensionally coherent conditional derivation or state the missing constitutive relation; preserve H1/H2 disagreement and do not infer RNA concentrations from DNA reads.
T05.reason: The principal missing link is the relation from composition-dependent partitioning to cavity formation; more descriptive time fitting cannot identify that mechanism.

reply.recognition: uncertain; no specific study recognized from the supplied input
reply.summary: The supplied image statistic is the arithmetic mean of per-droplet hollow-area ratios f(t), not an area-weighted ratio and not a concentration. B rises from 0.01381 at 0 h to 0.08918 at 24 h while A falls from 0.01487 to about 0.004. Only two independent preparations per condition; fields and objects are not independent preparation replicates. C01 shows B DNA read heterogeneity (reference fraction 0.9466; listed other reads sum 0.0500; frequency total 0.9966), but repeated/rearranged sequence alignment is nonunique and DNA read fractions do not establish RNA composition or activity. C02 describes the observed trajectory but its extrapolations are model-dependent: B predicts f(36 h)=0.1207 and f(48 h)=0.1563 under rise-to-plateau versus 0.1239 and 0.1635 under a linear description; these are not mechanism evidence. E02/fraction_dev has M near zero, M+L about 0.0445, M+S about 0.0941 endpoint hollow-area fractions, but no precise mixture ratios, matched carryover, or RNA yields. C04 has species-specific phase partition ratios that vary by tie-line (reference K about 239-525 on defined lines; variant K about 176-9032), with variant K undefined on line 0 because both measured concentrations are zero. C04 lacks phase volumes, time-resolved yields/flux, cavity-matched concentrations, and a mapping from concentration to image area. C03 confirms no persistent same-droplet hollow-state/area trajectories. Proposed gap: the missing constitutive bridge from RNA mixture composition and selective phase partitioning to internal RNA-poor cavity nucleation and area fraction.
